title: loc and iloc

cells.text: Back to the games! This lesson shows two tools that pick rows and columns at the same time: **iloc** (by position) and **loc** (by label or condition).

cells.prompt: Press Run to load the games table.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
df.head()

cells.text: Every row has a label on the left, called the **index**: 0, 1, 2 and so on. `df.iloc[0]` picks a row by its **position**, like a list, so `df.iloc[0]` is the first row. Notice the **square** brackets.

cells.prompt: Press Run to see the first row. It shows sideways, with the column names on the left.
What will this print? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: iloc can pick several rows and columns: `df.iloc[rows, columns]`. `:3` means "from the start up to 3, not including 3", so positions 0, 1 and 2. `df.iloc[:3, :2]` is the first 3 rows and the first 2 columns.

cells.prompt: Press Run to see the first 3 rows and first 2 columns.
Replace ___ so this shows the first 5 rows and the first 3 columns, then press Run.
hints: Use the same pattern as the columns part: a colon, then the number.

cells.text: **loc** picks by label or condition: `df.loc[rows, columns]`. The rows part can be a condition, and the columns part a list of names. So `df.loc[df["genre"] == "Shooter", ["title", "price"]]` filters and picks columns in one step.

cells.prompt: Press Run to show the title and price of the Shooter games.
Your turn: using loc, show the title and rating of the RPG games.
hints: Copy the cell above, then change Shooter to RPG and price to rating.

cells.prompt: Using loc, show the title and genre of every free game (price 0).
hints: Condition first: df["price"] == 0. Then a comma and the list of columns.

cells.text: loc can also pick one cell by its row **label** and column name: `df.loc[0, "title"]` is the title in the row labelled 0.

cells.prompt: What will this print? Remember, labels start at 0. Pick one, then press Run.

recap: iloc picks by position (like a list), and :3 means the first 3. loc picks by label or condition, with df.loc[rows, columns].
